items.title: US FAA begins 5-day audit of DGCA’s safety oversight system
points: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) will begin reassessing India’s aviation safety oversight system from Monday, officials said.
A team is scheduled to examine the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) over five days, focusing on its aircraft operations, airworthiness and personnel licensing processes.
The assessment, scheduled from November 16 to 20, is being conducted under the FAA’s International Aviation Safety Assessment (IASA) programme.

This programme evaluates whether a country’s civil aviation regulator complies with safety standards set by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO), a specialised agency of the United Nations.
India was last assessed in 2021, when its ICAO effective implementation (EI) score rose from 69.95% to 85.65%, indicating improved compliance with international aviation safety standards.
India currently holds Category 1 status under the FAA’s IASA programme.
Ahead of the assessment, the DGCA conducted a final round of inspections of all Indian airlines in the first week of October, following two earlier rounds in August and September.
